title: profile
description: A profile's public card, at the path `profile`: one per profile. A profile lives in one market, in one role; its label is market/role. Markets may add fields.

market.description: The market this profile lives in, as the markets directory spells it: the first half of its label.

role.description: Its role in that market: seller or buyer in a two-sided market, peer in a one-sided one. The second half of its label.

name.description: Optional. What the owner calls the profile. A card without a name is shown by its market and role.

inboxKey.description: Optional. The profile's inbox key, as an age post-quantum hybrid recipient (mlkem768x25519, 1,959 characters): what senders seal messages to, and others seal private records to. Without it, nobody can seal anything to this profile.

proofs.description: Optional. Proofs the profile shows, each one data anyone checks with its circuit's verifier (reputation/), for this profile's main key.

inbox.description: Optional. The profile's inbox: who may deliver a message to it on its hosts. Senders seal each message to inboxKey and to every reader, so a profile with an inbox also gives inboxKey. Without this field there is no inbox, and hosts refuse deliveries. A host refuses deliveries to an inbox it cannot read: a field, a rule or a value it does not know.

senders.description: Who may deliver: anyone, or a key holding a registry row from this issuer, under any label.

issuer.description: The issuer's key as a registry row holds it: x then y of its point on Baby Jubjub, each 32 bytes big-endian, as 128 characters of lowercase hex.

once.description: Optional. One message from each sender, ever: a host refuses a second from the same key for as long as it keeps the profile.

maxBytes.description: Optional. The largest message it takes, as canonical text in bytes. A host also takes messages only up to its own size.

readers.description: Optional. Read keys' public halves. A sender seals every message to inboxKey and to each of these, in one envelope, so a reader listed here can act on the inbox while the person is away. Each adds about 2 KB to every message.

proof.description: One proof, named by its circuit. A reader ignores a proof whose circuit it does not know, so a profile carrying a newer kind stays valid for an older app. A reputation proof and a person proof have the shapes below; another circuit's fields are its own.

circuit.description: The circuit that checks it. Today reputation (reputation/) and person (registry/).

reputation.description: A reputation proof (reputation/): the count-weighted score of profiles the person holds in an index's tree, shown on this profile, which profiles hidden. It counts only on the profile whose registry row sits at its stamp, made from the same secret as the profiles it counts: the prover's own. Everything its verifier takes but the main key, which is the profile's own.

index.description: The index's signing key: its address, base58.

root.description: The root of the index's tree the proof was made against: the 32 big-endian bytes the index signed, lowercase hex.

time.description: The time the index signed with the root, ms since 1970.

signature.description: The index's ed25519 signature over the root and the time, as reputation/ defines its signed bytes; 64 bytes in base64url without padding.

score.description: The score the proof shows: the count-weighted score of the profiles counted, times ten, rounded down.

stamp.description: The stamp of this profile's registry row, as the row holds it: 32 bytes big-endian, lowercase hex. The proof shows it came from the same secret as the profiles counted.

label.description: Present only when the proof shows one market: the label of the one profile counted, exactly as registered.

proof.description: The proof's three points, uncompressed: 256 bytes in base64url without padding. Eight numbers of 32 bytes big-endian, in snarkjs's names pi_a[0], pi_a[1], pi_b[0][1], pi_b[0][0], pi_b[1][1], pi_b[1][0], pi_c[0], pi_c[1]: the order Ethereum's and Solana's BN254 precompiles read.

person.description: A person proof (registry/), showing the profile's tier: this issuer signed a note at this tier for the person whose registry row, for this main key and this label, sits at this stamp. Everything registry/client's verifyTier takes but the main key, which is the profile's own.

issuer.description: The issuer's key as the row holds it: x then y of its point on Baby Jubjub, each 32 bytes big-endian, as 128 characters of lowercase hex.

label.description: The row's label, exactly as registered.

stamp.description: The stamp the row sits at, as the row holds it: 32 bytes big-endian, lowercase hex.

tier.description: The tier the issuer signed, in decimal: it can be any number below BN254's scalar order, and a record's numbers stop at 2^53 - 1. What it means is the issuer's.

proof.description: The proof's three points, uncompressed: 256 bytes in base64url without padding, in the reputation proof's order.

photo.description: Profile photo, named by the SHA-256 of its bytes.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the file, lowercase hex.

mimeType.description: The file's media type, type/subtype in lower case, such as image/jpeg. Which types to take is each host's own choice, and each reader's.

size.description: Bytes. How large a blob to take is each host's own choice, and each reader's.
